title: Emergency Pause Safety (Bounded Halt with Preserved Exit)

dascp.note: Establishes the BOUNDED form of emergency stop — the safety halt plus an auto-expiry or always-available exit; STRENGTHENS C29-S beyond the white-paper text, which mandates the kill-switch capability but not its boundedness.
System-level pause property; C30-S is the per-account refinement and requires its own scope.
System-level pause property; C31-S is the per-token refinement and requires its own scope.

iso20022.note: While paused, settlement transaction instructions are halted; the property constrains the processing of sese.023 instances within the paused mode and mandates either bounded auto-unpause or an always-available recovery edge so the pause cannot indefinitely freeze entitled exits.

iof.note: Bounded emergency-pause safety with a preserved exit is the formal content behind the block's explicit pause/kill-semantics requirement; the chain-agnostic-interface, verifiable-provenance, audited-code, and governed-upgrade ceremony facets of token/contract structure standardisation stay out-of-scope as data-standardisation and operational concerns.

descriptions.semantic: When the system is paused, value-moving state transitions are halted (safety); the pause can be entered only by an authorized pauser and lifted only by an authorized path; and — critically for the bounded form — the pause cannot deprive entitled users of their funds indefinitely: it either auto-expires after a bounded delay or always leaves a fund-recovery path (escape hatch) open. The unbounded form (halt with no time limit and no exit) is explicitly NOT this property and conflicts with exit liveness.
descriptions.system_theoretic: A mode-switched LTS with a `paused` control mode in which the transition relation is restricted to non-value-moving (and recovery) transitions, plus a meta-constraint that the system cannot remain in `paused` forever from the perspective of an entitled withdrawal (bounded sojourn or always-available exit edge).
descriptions.security: Pause is a double-edged control: it mitigates an active exploit by freezing damage, but an unbounded or mis-scoped pause is itself an attack surface — admin rug-by-freeze, key-compromise freeze, or incomplete coverage that pauses the wrong half and leaves the exploit live. The bounded form keeps the mitigation while denying the freeze-forever capability.
descriptions.execution_semantics: A `whenNotPaused` modifier gates value-moving functions; pause/unpause are privileged. The bounded guarantee adds either a timelocked auto-unpause (block.timestamp ≥ pausedAt + maxPause ⇒ effectively unpaused) or an always-callable forced-exit that ignores the pause flag for entitled withdrawals.
descriptions.formal_verification: Two obligations: (1) SAFETY — in the paused mode, no value-moving transition is enabled (model-check / SMT over the gated transition set, plus coverage that every value-moving selector is gated). (2) BOUNDED LIVENESS — the paused mode is not a permanent trap for entitled exits; requires the same fairness machinery as BPO:0002 (or a purely structural escape edge whose enabling is mode-independent, which makes it SMT-checkable).

formalization.signature: Mode ∈ {active, paused}; valueMoving ⊆ Op; recovery ⊆ Op; pausedAt: timestamp; maxPause: const.
formalization.first_order_logic:
Pause safety:  ∀ s,s',o . ( mode(s)=paused ∧ o ∈ valueMoving ∧ o ∉ recovery ∧ s --[o]--> s' ) → False  (such transitions are absent).
Coverage:  ∀ o ∈ valueMoving . gatedBy(o, whenNotPaused).
Bounded sojourn:  ∀ s . mode(s)=paused → ◇_{≤ maxPause} ( mode=active ∨ exitAvailable ).
Exit preservation:  ∀ s . entitledWithdrawal(p,s) → enabled(forcedExit(p), s)   (mode-independent).

temporal_logic.ltl: G( paused → ¬anyValueMove )   ∧   G( paused → F_{bounded} (active ∨ exitTaken) )
temporal_logic.ctl: AG( paused → AF active )   under the timelock/escape assumption
temporal_logic.fairness: For the structural-escape variant: none (escape edge is unconditionally enabled). For the auto-unpause variant: weak fairness on the clock/block production (BPO:0080).

formalization.state_machine: Two-mode automaton; `pause` and `unpause` are admin-gated edges; an auto-unpause edge fires when the clock guard holds; a forced-exit edge is enabled in both modes. The property is the conjunction of (no value-move edge from `paused`) and (paused is not absorbing for entitled exits).
formalization.type_theoretic: The pause capability is a bounded, possibly time-limited capability (a leasing/affine resource with an expiry), distinct from an unbounded admin capability.

relationships.note: The UNBOUNDED pause directly negates eventual-withdrawal. This bounded form is the designed resolution: keep the safety halt, deny freeze-forever.
An escape hatch realizes the exit-preservation clause and reconciles pause with exit liveness.
Pause/unpause authority is governed by access-control correctness.
Only the BOUNDED form mitigates this; the unbounded form CAUSES it.

attack_surface.pattern: pause with no time bound and no exit; equivalent to seizure of funds
attack_surface.notes: The whole reason this property is specified as bounded.

attack_surface.pattern: some value-moving path not gated; exploit continues while honest users are frozen
attack_surface.notes: Coverage obligation: enumerate and gate all value-moving selectors.

attack_surface.pattern: single guardian key freezes the system maliciously
attack_surface.notes: Multisig/timelock the pause authority; keep unpause less privileged or auto.

attack_surface.pattern: exploit re-fires in the block unpause executes

strategies.notes: Prove every value-moving method is gated and reverts when paused.
Check paused is not absorbing for entitled exits under the clock/escape assumption.

testability: all value-moving calls revert when paused

static: coverage check that no value-moving selector is ungated

assumptions.statement: Block clock advances so the auto-unpause guard can fire (only for the timelock variant).
Pause authority is not unilaterally controlled by a single untrusted key.

provenance.notes: Exists explicitly to host the safety/liveness tension with BPO:0002 and to show BPO records design tensions rather than hiding them.
